region.text: Lianchuan, Xiping and Ledu on the Huangshui, the Southern Liang's own land (the page's last 'few commanderies along the Huangshui River')

ledger.note: 397: Tufa Wugu proclaims the Southern Liang at Xiping. After Later Liang lost to Western Qin, Wugu 'proclaimed himself the Prince of Xiping' and changed the era name, a break from Later Liang; the Sixteen Kingdoms page: 'Tufa Wugu broke away and founded the Southern Liang (397-414)'. In 394 he had subjugated tribes in Qinghai and made Lianchuan his capital.
399: Lilugu succeeds Wugu, claims the title Prince of Hexi and moves the capital to Xiping (the text puts Wugu's move to Ledu in 398; the infobox has Ledu only in 399).
402: Rutan succeeds Lilugu, claims the title King of Liang and moves the capital back to Ledu.

region.text: Guzang (Wuwei), given to Rutan by Later Qin in 406

ledger.note: 406: Later Qin gives Rutan Guzang. Later Qin gave Rutan control of Guzang, which he later made his capital; he also allied with Western Liang against the Northern Liang. Later Qin's dossier dates the Hexi hand-over to 412 (confidence 1) but this page dates it to 406.
406: the capital moves to Guzang (infobox Guzang 406-410).

region.text: Guzang (Wuwei), given to Rutan by Later Qin in 406

ledger.note: 410: Guzang falls to the Northern Liang. Rebellions spread, the capital moved back to Ledu, and Guzang fell to Northern Liang. The Northern Liang page has Mengxun besiege Guzang in 410 and the inhabitants surrender in 411, with the capital there in 412.

ledger.note: 414: the Western Qin takes Ledu and the Southern Liang ends. 'The Western Qin attacked and captured Ledu, prompting the rest' of the territory to surrender and Rutan surrenders (Qifu Chipan poisoned him later that year); the Sixteen Kingdoms page: 'fell to the Western Qin in 414'.

notes: Cliopatria row: Southern Liang 397..413 (two shapes, both 31,085 km2). (1) The shape lies at Linxia-Lintao; the page's capitals and the 413 remnant are on the Huangshui near Xining and Ledu, so both shapes are marked wrong and replaced by a disc at Xining; the same disc is the Western Qin's 414 gain. (2) Years: the state ends 414 (Cliopatria 413). (3) Suspension: the infobox gives 'Existence: 397-404 and 408-414' and the text says the state was briefly discontinued after Rutan's 404 surrender to Later Qin; yet Later Qin gave him Guzang in 406 and he fought the Northern Liang from 407. The dossier keeps the state continuous, as Cliopatria does; the Later Qin dossier should hold the vassal relation of 404-408. (4) Disagreements between pages: Guzang lost 410 (Southern Liang page) or surrendered 411 (Northern Liang page); Later Qin's dossier has its Hexi hand-over to Southern Liang in 412 at confidence 1 whereas this page gives 406. (5) Cliopatria's Wikipedia field is 'Liang dynasty' (the 502-557 state); the opened article is 'Southern Liang (Sixteen Kingdoms)', used here; the Wikidata id is Cliopatria's and could not be checked. (6) Commanderies lost between 410 and 413 are not named; the Tuyuhun and the Western Qin attacked, undated, so no event is written. (7) Capital coordinates are the researcher's readings (the page gives none). Gazetteer names needed: Ledu (place, Haidong, Qinghai), Xiping (Xining), Lianchuan, Huangshui (river). Page budget: two pages.
